item.title: Be the cartographer of your own path
item.description:
Every creative journey starts with excitement. An incredible rush to create this new amazing thing, materializing before your very eyes. Sadly this feeling often withers away with time, when the project is big. What do you do then? What to do when the spark fades away?

Expectations vs reality

Every skill requires constant effort for progress. Often that progress is not linear though. Some days you feel you make no progress whatsoever, others you are at 200% productivity and feel fantastic (often after an energy drink).

item.title: This is Koz!
item.description:
The weird, yet charming idea.

Koz started as an ambitious university project for a pygame course. It was my first experience building a game outside of an engine and it was a wild one. I wanted to make something like a visual representation of what is going on in my head when playing Scoundrel and go off from there.

What is Scoundrel?

Scoundrel is a single player roguelike card game by Zach Gage and Kurt Bieg. You can have an awesome roguelike experience by yourself with a deck of cards and a counter. Ripple Shuffle & Roll’s tutorial

item.title: Your Great Work does not matter.
item.description:
“Create for the sake of creation, not for the sake of accomplishment, and you will be truly free from the shackles of normality.”

The Great Work

The Great Work is a term from Alchemy and Hermeticism, referring to a singular ultimate work of the practitioner. Their Magnum Opus. The work that defines them and drives them to discover the hidden secrets of the universe.

We use the same mentality for our own creative works, striving for this ultimate goal, trying to be the very best.

item.title: The True Value of R&D
item.description:
Research and Development AKA R&D is a common branch in many big companies dedicated to “playing around” with ideas until they strike something good.

Experimentation is not treated as an afterthought, but as a necessity for the survival of the company.

Companies have a metric called “R&D Intensity”, the ratio of revenue spent on R&D. The riskier, or “growth oriented” the company is, the bigger the R&D intensity. Biotech is naturally a leader in the field.

item.title: Code Like a Photographer
item.description:
I’m a sort of experienced programmer by now, with a couple years under my belt working on various projects, both professional and personal. Wouldn’t say I’m great, but I’ve been around the block.

In my development journey I never really found the time or motivation to re-write a whole project from scratch, since I never really found a reason. It’s already done after all, I’ve built the thing, so logically I should know it by heart. Re-doing the whole process would just be a waste of time. Does sound legit, doesn’t it?
